pass_a_gloss: These things he took away to the people of the Jews and to the defilement according to Christ for they thought he had citizenship only on earth. They will not simply receive but they will inherit. The ungodly even if they are exalted will not become greater but their dishonor will become greater. For just as someone who is ugly and distorted if he is exalted does not become glorious but is dishonored more his shame is made clear to more people so also God exalts the ungodly in order that their shamelessness may become manifest. Pharaoh was also exalted but so that he might have the whole world as an accuser. It should be noted that he calls the law a good gift because of the one who receives gifts in bosom unjustly. This one however leaves behind a heap the one who transgresses the law. Is the law what he says or what he himself kept? And how is it to enclose thoughts with it? For you need much safety since many things plot against such a possession. But if it is up to us to enclose it and virtues are up to us then virtues are the fences that exalt the knowledge of God such as exercise and study and another of the virtues which the one who keeps wisdom honors. And the reward is to be lifted up to it and to be enclosed by it in the supramundane pasture.
pass_b_english: These things he took away to the people of the Jews and to the defilement according to Christ, for they thought he had citizenship only on earth. They will not simply receive, but they will inherit. The ungodly, even if they are exalted, do not become greater; rather, their dishonor becomes greater. For just as someone who lifts up a person who is ugly and twisted does not glorify him but dishonors him more, making his shame clear to more people, so also God exalts the ungodly in order that their shamelessness may become manifest. Pharaoh was also exalted, but so that he might have the whole world as an accuser. It should be noted that he calls the law a good gift because of the one who receives gifts in the bosom unjustly. This one, however, leaves behind a heap—the one who transgresses the law. Is the law what he says, or what he himself kept? And how is it to enclose thoughts with it? For you need much safety, since many things plot against such a possession. But if it is up to us to enclose it, and virtues are up to us, then virtues are the fences that exalt the knowledge of God, such as exercise, study, and another of the virtues' steps, which the one who keeps wisdom honors. And the reward is to be lifted up to it and to be enclosed by it in the supramundane pasture.
